To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chemical modification of LiFePO 4 by substitution of the Li and Fe sites by other cations can lead to the improvement of the electrochemical performance of the olivines, which makes them more promising for use as cathode materials in lithium ion batteries.
the substitution of iron by transition metals (Mn, Co and Ni) in LiFePO4 leads to a decrease of the activation energy for lithium ion diffusion, which is beneficial for the battery performance.

(i) LiFePO4 substituted with Li+ and Fe3+ by Al3+ and W6+ forms a narrow solid solution, (ii) LiFePO3 substituted with Li+ by Zr4+ forms a narrow and LiFePO4 with Fe3+ by Mn2+, Co3+ and Ni2+ forms a large solid solution and (iii) substitution of Fe by 3d transition metals does not influence the electrical conductivity of LiFePO3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a series of LiFePO₄-based compounds with different cations in the Li and Fe sub-lattices.
the possibility of substitution of lithium and iron in LiFePO4 by cations of other metals.
the synthesis of LiFePO₄ and its solid solutions with cationic dopants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the substitution of Fe by Mn, Co and/or Ni in the LiFePO4 lattice leads to a considerable improvement of the electrochemical performance of this material.
the substitution of iron in LiFePO4 leads to an increase of the battery performance, while the substitution of lithium leads to the opposite effect.
the chemical modification of LiFePO₄ by introduction of cations in the Li and Fe sub-lattices is a promising approach to improve the electrochemical properties of this material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LiFePO4 can be modified by substitution of both the Li and Fe sub-lattices by a number of cations.
a substitution of Li and Fe sub-lattices by other cations can be a very efficient tool for tuning the physicochemical and electrochemical properties of the LiFePO4 cathode material.
the substitution of Li+ and Fe3+ in LiFePO4 by Al3+, Co3+, Mn3+, Ni2+ and W6+ leads to a considerable decrease in the discharge capacity of the cathode material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrochemical properties of the LiFePO4-based olivine cathodes are strongly influenced by the nature of the Fe substitution.
the chemical modification of the Li and Fe sub-lattices by doping with Al3+, Zrx4+, W6+, Mn2+, Co2+, and Ni2+ cations leads to an improvement in the electrochemical properties of olivine LiFePO4.

the chemical modification of olivines by introduction of cations in Li and Fe sites can be used to improve their transport properties, but the improvement of electrochemical properties depends on the nature of the dopant.
